text:
izzy: quick note from today's rollout: when new GPU slabs come online the continuous-batcher sees a short period of noisy tails. observed 30-70ms tail spikes for ~3-5 minutes. likely KV-cache cold + a wave of tiny single-slot batches. thinking we should design a node-join "warmup" mode for lanes to reduce oscillation.

kai: can you paste a minimal trace? curious if it's predominantly KV fetch latency or scheduling preemption churn.

izzy: snippet attached below. two things stand out: (1) cold-key fetches that take 10-20ms, (2) a flurry of batch_sz=1 fastpath reqs around same time stealing slots.

[TRACE] req=tn-12 batch_sz=2 wait=1ms kv_fetch=18ms schedule_wait=9ms
[TRACE] req=tn-99 batch_sz=1 wait=0ms kv_hit=1 schedule_wait=4ms preempted_by=tn-12

yusuf: idea: implement per-lane "join_warmup" state. during warmup we (a) slightly increase coalesce window for those lanes, (b) reduce fastpath throttle (i.e., delay 1-slot immediate dispatch), and (c) prefer packing small requests into permissive microbatches.

kai: agree but need opt-out for latency-critical tenants. lanes could carry a tag (latency_sensitive: true) to skip warmup. also prefer to scope to the slab that just joined (topology-aware) so we don't impact unrelated lanes.

izzy: rough config proto: warmup_mode {
  enabled: true
  estimate_seconds: 90
  coalesce_add_ms: 10
  permissive_pack: true
  decay_seconds: 180
  user_visible_cap_ms: 60
}

kaI: two tuning knobs: estimate_seconds should come from an online metric (KV miss rate -> keys/sec warming), and coalesce_add_ms should be bounded by user_visible_cap_ms. also add validation: decay_seconds >= estimate_seconds.

yusuf: operational guardrails: 1) if a lane's tiny_request_ratio > 40% for >15s, treat it as inherently small-req and skip warmup; 2) if SLA tail breach detected, abort warmup for affected lanes immediately.

izzy: observability: propose a composite "warmup_risk_score" per node combining kv_warm_pct (inverted), tiny_req_rate, and preempt_count. expose in console and allow smoothing to be gated by score > threshold.

devops-bot: note: we already export node.kv_warm_pct and node.batch_preempt_rate metrics. opened INF-3350 to add warmup_risk_score in dashboard.

kai: longer-term: opportunistic rebalance. once a slab appears we can move a controlled fraction of non-critical tenants to it to accelerate KV population. must be canaryed: move 1% of batch-friendly tenants, watch kv_warm_pct and tail, then continue. add hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping.

yusuf: routing change complexity: ensure we don't violate per-tenant affinity or stickiness. add a migration policy that respects tenant tags (no move for pinned tenants) and uses a slow ramp.

izzy: prototype plan: 1) implement warmup state + config and warmup_risk_score metric 2) run offline sims (48h) with mixed traces including 5% micro-tenant traffic and cold-kv patterns 3) if sims show reduced tail, do a small canary rebalance experiment.

kai: also add a sim scenario with high tiny-req tenants to validate the admission rule. i'll help craft traces.

devops-bot: INF-3350 created; added watchers izzy,kai,yusuf.

izzy: thanks all. i'll post sim results in this thread next week. ":rocket:"
